line.comment: * Task 0.
* Expanded 2.2.1 draft: Independent homebase claim ledger based on Renegades sector discovery.
* Retains existing Explorer movement, avoidance, and homebound escape behavior.
* FoF introduced similar coordination/avoidance concepts; audit their remaining provenance separately.
* Cartographer.
* We create a special array to handle explorer sync, for performance purposes. See Mayhem.GetExplorers.
* Initialized here because the main loop reads variables assigned in subroutines.
* MSCI may otherwise report them as unassigned during compilation.
* Recover any assignment left by a previous instance of this worker.
* Zero Hour: hard difficulty allows Explorers to claim and conquer neutral sectors.
* Release abandoned assignments when returning to the dispatch cycle.
* Zero Hour: hard and insane difficulty allow Explorers to claim and conquer neutral sectors.
* ZH 1.8: only 2% chance for such opportunistic claims.
* ZH 2.0: reduced further to 0.2% but no longer limited to early game.
* Add-Ons 1.3: Chance increased to 1% on insane.
* Sector is Unknown.
* Once there we need to check again because we didn't already claim on departure like Battlegroups do
* Mordan9
* Requirement: a ship is considered capable if it has at least 65% hull (consistency with OCV virus takeover repair and Pirate claiming).
* If the factory was destroyed or the explorer was reassigned, restart immediately.
* Same homebase, has no eligible sector.
* Expanded 2.2.1: Resolve a completed attack interrupt.
* The original mapping movement may resume after FleeHome inside !ship.signal.attacked finishes.
* Do not map the sector in which the attack occurred.
* The sector may have changed owner, blacklist status, or satellite coverage during travel.
* The satellite goes down the moment the ship arrives.
* This increases Explorer efficiency (it can keep moving between sectors rather than spend extra time at the destination sector) at the cost of satellite safety.
* Drop a satellite and set it to be owned by the player if this is the NPC doing us a favor.
* Expanded 2.2.1: Distinguish actual fire from hostile combat-capable ships.
* Under fire: return home. Hostile presence alone: select another mapping target.
* Nobody has fired: keep the remaining satellites and take the next target instead of flying
* home and dumping them. CheckAvoid: keeps this sector off the list for the next 30 minutes.
* Failed docking must not enter the long idle-at-home wait.
* Player: wait 1-2 minutes. This is an exception to the parity rule, because NPCs do not lose satellites to periodic removal.
* Therefore, they do not need to work as often as player explorers. NPCs wait 10x longer.
* Expanded 2.2.1: Evaluate combat capability instead of relative speed. This is because slower enemies in OOS can still kill.
* $underAttack means an actionable threat exists; leave this sector.
* $underFire means the Explorer was attacked; return home.
* Hostile armed presence alone sets $underAttack but not $underFire.
* Actual attacks take priority over proactive threat classification.
* OOS combat can threaten the Explorer without a conventional pursuit.
* Find hostile ships, then check whether they have usable armament.
* Freighters are excluded from proactive avoidance; actual attacks still count.
* Compatible missiles count only when actually present in cargo.
* End enemy check.
* Expanded 2.2.1: Preserve 2.2's response to actual attacks versus hostile presence.
* Actual fire sends the ship home; hostile presence alone permits continued mapping.
* Avoidance state remains per-ship and does not modify global routing.
* Avoid dangerous sectors for 30 minutes of playing time, then reconsider them.
* 30 minutes because of uncertainty: wait long enough for a threat to clear.
* Check if a satellite is present or not.
* For the AI, we manage sector blacklist here. Blacklist Yaki sectors as a non-Yaki because of universal Yaki hostility.
* already handled by Zero Hour Core AI update
* SWmM3.IsSatWhitelisted is used only by the player, not by NPCs.
* Only after hostile sector filtering, hostility, and blacklisting do we consider favor.
* No second satellite where we already have one.
* Expanded claim ledger: each homebase stores sector -> assigned Explorer.
* Cache reachable candidates and short-lived negative eligibility results separately.
* Neither cache stores reservations or consumes selected sectors.
* Cache the candidate SET, not its order: Phanon sees the whole galaxy,
* and every Explorer still needs its own nearest-first ordering.
* Do not publish a snapshot for a destroyed or changed homebase.
* Copy before sorting: sorting must never mutate a homebase-shared array.
* Get shared, authoritative claims once; the table is modified in place.
* Cache only negative eligibility for 120 seconds. Positive results
* are always checked live before claiming and again upon arrival.
* Check candidates in small batches; yield once per 8 sectors rather than
* delaying every cached rejection. This bounds per-frame work at scale.
* Skip active claims before expensive eligibility checks.
* Most sectors are already monitored late-game; share short-lived
* negative results so each Explorer does not repeat the same checks.
* Eligibility scripts may yield, so revalidate the homebase.
* A newly valid sector should no longer carry its negative hint.
* A competing Explorer might have claimed while CheckSector yielded.
* No waits or script calls between this check and claim recording.
* Claims are independent of both caches. Verify the current holder.
* Relinquish only our own reservation, never another ship's replacement claim.
* Unload wares and repair only after successful docking.
